summary: At 18 minutes after the fault start, stripper pressure (XMEAS(16)) rose 27.7 σ and compressor work (XMEAS(20)) rose 13.1 σ, indicating a rapid up‑trend in upstream units. This pattern matches the historic incident where an A/C feed ratio step occurred while B composition stayed constant.

A deviation was detected 48 min after fault start, marked by a sharp rise in purge gas analysis (component B) (XMEAS(30)) followed by increased purge rate and valve position. The pattern matches past fault 2 (B composition step, A/C ratio constant) in the Feeds unit.

A deviation was detected 6 minutes after the fault start in the Reactor cooling water flow (XMV(10)), rising upward with a magnitude of 11.7 σ. This aligns with a known fault (fault 4) related to a reactor cooling water inlet temperature step.

At ~48 minutes after the fault start, reactor, separator, and stripper pressures rose sharply (up to ~15σ). Later, compressor work dropped and temperatures rose, indicating a system-wide pressure upset likely linked to a condenser cooling water inlet temperature step.

A significant drop in A feed (stream 1) was detected immediately, followed by a large increase in the feed valve opening and downstream compressor disturbances. The pattern matches the known fault 6 (A feed loss) in the Feeds unit.

At the start of run‑07 a large drop in the A and C feed (XMEAS(4) down 13.2 σ) was detected immediately, followed by rapid pressure increases in the reactor, separator and stripper (up ~28 σ) and a rise in reactor cooling water outlet temperature. The pattern matches fault 7 (C header pressure loss in the feed unit).

At ~84 minutes after the fault start, both feed analysis signals showed significant deviations (component C down 17.3σ, component A up 10.8σ) in the Feeds unit, matching the pattern of fault 2 (B composition step, A/C ratio constant). This suggests a likely issue with the B composition step affecting feed streams.

A significant upward deviation was observed in the Stripper temperature (XMEAS(18)), reaching 10.7 σ 291 minutes after the fault onset. This is the earliest and largest signal, indicating a likely issue in the Stripper unit.

At 33 min after the fault onset the reactor cooling water flow (XMV(10)) spiked upward to 17.1 σ above normal, and later the reactor temperature (XMEAS(9)) dropped 15.5 σ. This pattern matches fault 11 (reactor cooling water inlet temperature random variation) in the library.

At ~63 min after the fault start, both separator temperature (XMEAS(11)) and condenser cooling water outlet temperature (XMEAS(22)) dropped sharply, with deviations of 37.9 σ and 28.4 σ respectively. This pattern matches a known incident (fault 12) caused by random variation in the condenser cooling water inlet temperature in the Separator and condenser unit.

At ~141 min after the fault start, major pressure drops were observed in the Stripper (XMEAS(16)), Reactor (XMEAS(7)) and Separator/Condenser (XMEAS(13)), each deviating ~39 σ below normal. The deviations then propagated to steam flow and valve actions in the Stripper later on.

At ~6 min after the fault onset the reactor cooling water outlet temperature rose 19.7 σ, followed by large increases in cooling water flow (24.0 σ) and reactor temperature (23.6 σ) by 15 min. This pattern matches fault 14, a sticking reactor‑cooling water valve, affecting the Reactor cooling unit.

A significant upward deviation was observed in Stripper steam flow (XMEAS(19)), reaching 9.9 σ 588 minutes after the fault onset. This pattern matches a historical incident (fault 7) linked to C header pressure loss in the Feeds unit.

At 69 minutes after the fault start, the reactor cooling water outlet temperature (XMEAS(21)) dropped sharply, deviating 118.5 σ below normal. This early, large negative deviation matches fault 17 from the library with high similarity.

At ~261 min after the fault start, the condenser cooling water outlet temperature (XMEAS(22)) dropped sharply (‑50 σ) followed by a separator temperature drop (XMEAS(11), ‑30 σ) and later a separator pressure rise (XMEAS(13), +56 σ). These deviations match the pattern of past fault 18.

A significant down‑trend was detected in the compressor recycle valve (21.5 σ) followed by drops in separator pressure (14 σ) and compressor work (19 σ). The deviation began around minute 244‑246 and was detected 252 min after fault start.

Significant down‑trends have been observed in stripper pressure, reactor pressure, and separator pressure, with deviations up to 9 σ. Additional drops in reactor level, stripper steam flow, and the stripper steam valve follow, indicating a broad pressure loss across the front‑end units.
